title: Derived semilinear transitions compose
statement:
For l≤m≤n, the derived transition n→m followed by scalar restriction of m→l and the canonical restriction compositor is precisely the actual derived transition n→l.

Precise formal conclusion with its module-variable context (notation is that of the cited statement dependencies):
```lean
universe u v w
variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
  [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{w} RingCat.{w})]
  [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{w}] [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{w}]
  (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf J CommRingCat.{w})
theorem systemDerivedTransition_comp {l m n : ℕ} (h : l ≤ m) (k : m ≤ n)
    (M : DerivedCategory (StrictRingSystem B)) :
    (systemDerivedTransition B k).app M ≫
      (systemRestriction B k).mapDerivedCategory.map ((systemDerivedTransition B h).app M) ≫
      (systemDerivedRestrictionComposition B h k).hom.app
        ((derivedSystemEvaluation B l).obj M) =
    (systemDerivedTransition B (h.trans k)).app M
```

proof.text: Use localization uniqueness and postcompose with invertible target evaluation and restriction factorizations. The canonical restriction compositor has the forward factorization formula. Naturality of restriction factorization and the two transition representative formulas reduce both sides to Q of the strict composition law, which holds termwise on sections.
